To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the insurer’s optimal investment and reinsurance strategies depend on the interest rate model, the inflation rate model, the reinsurance premium rate, the risk aversion coefficient, and the initial wealth.

(1) The insurer is willing to transfer more risk to a reinsurer if the insurer’s investment opportunity set is expanded; (2) The optimal reinsurance and investment strategy of an insurer are affected by the stochastic nature of the interest rate and the inflation rate; and (3) In general, the optimal reinsurance and the optimal investment strategy are affected by the level of risk aversion of the insurer.

the stochastic interest rate assumption has significant impact on the insurer’s investment and reinsurance decision making, which in turn affects the optimal risk retention and the optimal risk transfer.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the optimal reinsurance-ininvestment problem of an insurer under stochastic interest rate and inflation models.
an optimal reinsurance–investment problem for an insurer under stochastic interest and inflation rate.
the study of optimal decision making of a classical insurance problem, namely, the optimal reinsurance-investing problem, under two different stochastic interest models.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, for the insurer, the Ho– Lee interest rate model is more favorable than the Vasicek interest rate model in the sense that it leads to higher utility of terminal wealth, and thus higher expected utility.
stochastic interest rates should be taken into account when the insurer makes investment and reinsurance policy decisions.
the Ho–Lee interest rate model provides better approximation to the optimal decision making process of the insurer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Ho–Lee interest rate model is more suitable than the Vasicek interest rate model in modeling the optimal decision making of insurers in the presence of inflation risk.
stochastic interest rate modeling has significant impacts on optimal decision making, which may not be ignored in practice.

the insurer’s investment strategy is sensitive to the interest rate model, and the insurer’s investment in the share is more significant than the investment in the bond in the Ho–Lee interest rate environment, whereas the investment in the share and the investment in the bonds are comparable when the insurer’s investment is made under the Vasicek interest rate environment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the insurer’s optimal decision is highly sensitive to the choice of interest rate model.
, when the insurer’s investment horizon is relatively long, the Ho–-Lee model should be preferred to the Vasicek one in the study of an optimal investment-reinsurance problem.
the stochastic interest rate modeling assumption has a significant impact on the optimal decision making of an insurer.
